Today's international headlines:
- Israel confirms it opened fire on vehicle carrying five-year-old Hind Rajab in Gaza: She initially survived the attack but her body was recovered days later in Gaza City in 2024.
- Sacked Ukrainian defence minister calls for presidential election: Martial law has been in place in Ukraine since February 2022, under which elections are suspended.
- Mushroom murderer trial undermined by 'catastrophic' hotel mix-up, appeal court told: Erin Patterson's defence team appeal against her conviction for killing relatives with a beef Wellington laced with toxic mushrooms.
- Trump pauses new tariffs on Canada for three days, saying deal close: The US president says the two sides are finalising documents to avert import taxes targeting a range of Canadian goods.
- South Korea shortens war games with US, citing Washington request: It comes after Trump announced plans to curtail joint military exercises with South Korea, citing a "very good" relationship with North Korea's Kim Jong Un.
- Ukrainian man arrested in Croatia over Nord Stream pipeline blasts: The man is alleged to have been one of the scuba divers who planted explosives on the pipelines in 2022.
- Six tourists and pilot killed in Kenya helicopter crash: The Aircraft Accident Investigation Department tells the BBC the nationalities are yet to be confirmed.
- Apparent human remains found in US reservoir as water levels hit record low: The skeletal remains in Lake Mead include what appears to be a human jaw with teeth attached, a witness says.
- Head-on collision between bus and lorry in Brazil kills more than 20: It is not yet clear what caused the two vehicles to crash into each other in the early hours of Wednesday morning.
- Liberia agrees to accept 1,200 foreign deportees from the US: Liberia says the deal is a "humanitarian arrangement" and is receiving no compensation.
- US condemns 'unnecessary escalation' after Israeli airstrikes on Syrian airbase: Damascus called the attacks "an unjustified act of aggression" that imperilled regional security.
- Christian metal band Demon Hunter sue Netflix over KPop Demon Hunters: The band say they face "an existential crisis" after the success of the K-pop-inspired Netflix film.
